episodes.162051: An upper low and weak cold front produced showers and a few thunderstorms during the late afternoon and early evening hours from middle Tennessee into north Alabama. One of the showers produced rotation, exhibited a rotating wall cloud and produced a couple of funnel clouds in western Madison County just north of Madison near Capshaw.  The funnels were videoed and sent via social media. A Baron Critical Weather Institute mesonet camera atop Rainbow Mountain captured this event as well with a well-defined wall cloud and small funnels.
episodes.162461: A trough positioned across offshore Georgia waters and through western Charleston County along with light southerly winds led to conditions favorable for waterspouts near the southeast South Carolina coast.
episodes.163291: A pulse-storm resulted in a brief tornado in a field. It was confirmed via a photograph by a storm spotter which showed a cloud of dirt being spun-up.
episodes.163408: Heavy rain brought flash flooding to central Arkansas.  A locally extreme rainfall event provided several inches on October 2. A few rounds of thunderstorms moved across the area bringing some beneficial rainfall to the state. While portions of northern Pulaski and Lonoke Counties picked up around 8 inches of rain, most reporting sites across the state received less than one half inch. A few exceptions included Camden (Ouachita County) where 3.00 inches of rain occurred and Newport (Jackson County) where 2.59 inches of rain fell.
episodes.163466: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of east central Illinois during the afternoon of October 3rd.  One of the storms produced a brief tornado in a corn field in Iroquois County.  No damage was reported.
episodes.163643: A weak tornado impacted Springfield Township in Oakland county.
episodes.163768: On the evening of October 3rd, lightning stuck a house in Big Island, VA. The strike blew open the bathroom wall and caused a small fire.
episodes.163997: A few small, rotating storms developed during the afternoon hours on October 3 in the Nashville metro area. One storm produced a brief EF-0 tornado in Wilson County.

events.narrative: Rounds of heavy rain over the same area lead to flooding on Somers Avenue.
This was the rainfall total from 7 pm CST to 845 pm CST.
Silver Creek Drive was flooded with a vehicle almost completely submerged in the water.
Hillard Road flooded and one vehicle washed off the road. The driver was rescued.
U.S Highway 67 northbound was closed at this location due to high water across all lanes.
Sandlewood Drive was flooded with two vehicles almost completely submerged.

events.narrative: A picture received via Twitter showed a waterspout off the coast of Kiawah Island and Folly Beach. A faint spray ring was seen below the condensation funnel.

A trained spotter photographed a brief tornado in a farm field north of US 20 and Walnut Grove intersection. The photo showed dirt being kicked up in the farm field. The tornado lasted about one minute. No damage was reported.
Trained spotters reported a brief tornado touched down in a corn field northwest of Ashkum.  No known damage was caused by the tornado.

A small weak EF-0 tornado touched down along John Hager Road in southwest Mount Juliet then moved northeast across I-40. Several videos of the tornado were taken in this area. The tornado apparently lifted before crossing Central Pike then briefly touched down again on Hatcher Road where it blew down a few trees. Max winds were estimated at 60 mph.
Damage included: numerous large tree limbs broken off, few small trees uprooted, and very minor siding damage to two homes. Max winds were estimated at 65 mph.
Lightning struck a house in the 1200 block of Ivory Grove Road. The lightning blew out the bathroom wall and caused a small fire. Damage values are estimated.

Several reports and videos were received of brief funnel clouds just north of U.S. Highway 72 in the Madison-Capshaw area.  No damage was reported. A Baron Critical Weather Institute mesonet camera atop Rainbow Mountain captured this event as well with a well-defined wall cloud and small funnels.  A social media video also showed a rotating wall cloud very low to the ground with a brief funnel in this same general area.
